recordStatementVerbatim: Can two distinct central binomial coefficients have exactly the same prime divisors?

formalizedStatement: For all distinct a, b >= 0 the central binomial coefficients C(2a,a) and C(2b,b) do not have exactly the same set of prime divisors, i.e. rad(C(2a,a)) != rad(C(2b,b)) where rad(x) is the product of the distinct primes dividing x.
formalizationCarrier: the Lean theorem statement of the T4 formalize node and the base/step recheck scope of the four review nodes

definitions.term: have exactly the same prime divisors
definitions.recordReading: the question's phrase, matching the prime-support results of [EGRS75]
definitions.formalizedReading: equal radical (set of prime divisors), NOT equal factorization with multiplicities
definitions.note: The distinction matters: equality of the full prime factorization would be a different (trivial) question. The formal statement must use the set reading.

definitions.recordReading: central binomial coefficients C(2a,a), C(2b,b) of the record's title
definitions.note: Central binomial coefficients are strictly increasing in a, so numerical distinctness is automatic; the formal statement keeps a != b as the index condition.

definitions.recordReading: [EGRS75] 'On the prime factors of C(2n,n)' (Math. Comp. (1975), 83-92)
definitions.formalizedReading: the set of primes p for which the p-adic valuation of C(2n,n) is positive
definitions.note: The formalization's base lemmas must be stated in this form to match the cited result.
